name: the Russian Synodal Bible
title: Synodal (RUSV) against BHSA and Nestle 1904
notes: Russian «и», «а», «но» link to וְ/καί when they render it.
A Russian possessive or pronoun («его», «Свой») links to the original word that carries that suffix or pronoun.

The Synodal translation follows the Septuagint in places: words or clauses it has from the Greek Old Testament have no Hebrew counterpart and stay unlinked; a Hebrew word it renders after the Septuagint's reading is still its counterpart when the meaning corresponds.
The Synodal New Testament follows the Received Text, so a Russian word with no Nestle 1904 counterpart is not an error: leave it unlinked.

The corpus numbers this text's chapters as the English Bibles do, but psalm titles are part of verse 1 here while the Hebrew numbers the title as a verse of its own; the frame line shows which Hebrew verses each verse maps to, and a link into the next Hebrew verse there is not a link to the wrong verse.
